Norway under Magnus, brought back from Gardariki to rule (N1: 1034; Sweyn and Ælfgifu fled in autumn 1035)

capitals.name: Winchester
capitals.note: The infobox of N1 gives Winchester, England, as the capital; Denmark and Norway were governed through regents (N2: Ulf Jarl in Denmark from 1020; Sweyn Knutsson in Norway).

rulers.name: Cnut the Great
rulers.note: King of England from 1016, of Denmark from 1018, of Norway from 1028; died 12 November 1035 at Shaftesbury (N2). The infobox of N1 lists Sweyn Forkbeard (1013-1014), Cnut (1016-1035) and Harthacnut (1040-1042).

keyframe_review.note: 215,566 km2, bounding box -5.77E..16.10E, 49.98N..57.77N: England and Denmark with its eastern provinces. N1: Cnut acquired England after Assandun (1016) and Denmark in 1018 (infobox; the text has him going to Denmark 'in 1019 to claim the throne'). The page gives no area in its infobox, so the figure is unchecked. The claim to 'part of Sweden' (the 1027 title, N2) is not drawn.

484,573 km2: Norway added. N2: 'In 1028, Cnut set off from England to Norway, and the city of Trondheim, with a fleet of fifty ships', and 'the expulsion of Olaf Haraldsson in 1028'. Cliopatria's Old Kingdom of Norway row also has a shape 1015-1039, so Norway is drawn twice in 1028-1039.

The shape runs to 1039 but N1 says the empire 'collapsed immediately once Cnut died in 1035': Norway is lost in autumn 1035, England passes to Harold Harefoot (regent 1035-1037, king until 1040, N2) and Denmark to Harthacnut. The shape holds for 1034 and 1035 only. For 1036-1039 Cliopatria has no Danish row, so Denmark under Harthacnut is undrawn unless another dossier covers it (see notes).

correction.text: unchanged shape; the years should read 1034..1035 (Cnut died 12 November 1035)

region.text: England, won by Cnut in 1016, and Denmark, taken up in 1018

ledger.note: 1018: Cnut, already king of England, becomes king of Denmark and rules both. N2: 'Harald II died in 1018, and Cnut went to Denmark to affirm his succession to the Danish crown.' N1 infobox agrees on 1018; its text has Cnut going to Denmark 'in 1019 to claim the throne' and Harald dying in 1018 or 1019.

1028: Cnut takes Norway. N2: 'In 1028, Cnut set off from England to Norway, and the city of Trondheim, with a fleet of fifty ships', after 'the expulsion of Olaf Haraldsson in 1028'; N1 has him acclaimed king at Nidaros (Trondheim). Norway stayed a kingdom under Cnut's son Sweyn and his mother Ælfgifu (N1, N2), not annexed: the old-kingdom-of-norway dossier records the same pair of events as an occupation by the North Sea Empire.

region.text: the kingdom of Malcolm II of Scotland

ledger.note: 1031: Malcolm II of Scotland submits to Cnut. N2: 'In 1031, Malcolm II of Scotland also submitted to him.' N1 says Cnut made vassals of three Scottish kings after his 1027 visit to Rome, without a year. The land is read as Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba.

Autumn 1035: Norway slips away from Cnut's sons. N1: by winter 1033 Sweyn and Ælfgifu were forced to leave Trondheim and in autumn 1035 they fled Norway; in 1034 Magnus was brought back from Gardariki to rule (Magnus the Good's own page, opened for norway-denmark, has him returning in 1035).

region.text: the kingdom of Malcolm II of Scotland

ledger.note: 12 November 1035: Cnut's death ends the submission of the Scottish kings. Page silent: neither page says what became of the 1031 submission; it is closed with the empire.

region.text: England, Denmark and Norway, divided among Harold, Harthacnut and Magnus

ledger.note: 12 November 1035: Cnut dies and the North Sea Empire falls apart. N2: 'Cnut died on 12 November 1035 in Shaftesbury, Dorset.' N1: the empire 'collapsed immediately once Cnut died in 1035'; Harthacnut succeeded in Denmark, Harold Harefoot ruled England (regent 1035-1037, king until 1040), Magnus held Norway. N1's infobox end of 1042 is Harthacnut's death, after he had regained England in 1040 (see denmark-england).

wars.name: Cnut against Olaf II and Anund Jacob (Battle of the Helgeå)
wars.outcome: Olaf II attacked Denmark; N1 has Cnut defeating him at the Helgeå while noting that Anglo-Saxon sources credit Anund Jacob with the victory; no frontier moved.
wars.note: N1 dates the attack to 1025 or 1026; N2 has the battle 'probably in 1026'. After it Cnut claimed to be king 'of some of the Swedes' (N2, 1027 letter); no Swedish land is drawn.

wars.name: Cnut's conquest of Norway
wars.outcome: Olaf Haraldsson expelled; Cnut acclaimed at Nidaros and Sweyn Knutsson set up as his ruler in Norway (N2 puts the arrangement after Stiklestad, 1030).

wars.name: Magnus's return to Norway
wars.outcome: Magnus, Olaf's son, is brought back from Gardariki; Sweyn Knutsson and Ælfgifu flee in autumn 1035 and Norway leaves the empire.
wars.note: N1 gives 1034 for Magnus's recall; Magnus the Good's own page (opened for norway-denmark) says he returned in 1035.

certainty.note: A union of three crowns; the English and Danish edges are old frontiers, the Norwegian and Scottish edges are the limit of Cnut's authority, none fixed by treaty.

notes:
DECISION: the North Sea Empire is Cnut's personal union of England, Denmark and (1028-1035) Norway. Cliopatria ends it in 1039; both pages opened put its collapse at Cnut's death in 1035 (N1: the empire 'collapsed immediately once Cnut died in 1035'), so the dossier ends 12 November 1035. The 1036-1039 years are not this state's: Harold Harefoot ruled England, Harthacnut Denmark (N2), Magnus Norway. Cliopatria nevertheless draws the whole empire shape to 1039 because it has NO Danish row between 1018 and 1055 and no England row between 1018 and 1045; Denmark in 1036-1039 therefore has no drawing unless the kingdom-of-denmark dossier (eu-14, another part) supplies one, or the renderer keeps this shape's Danish core. The orchestrator should settle who draws Denmark 1036-1055.
START: the dossier starts at 1018 (Cnut becomes king of Denmark). England alone under Cnut from 1016 is the Kingdom of England's, and 1013-1014 under Sweyn Forkbeard (N1 infobox) is not drawn. N1's own period is 1013-1042.
NOT ON THE PAGES: any area figure (N1 infobox gives none), the Battle of the Holy River (1026/1027 in other sources; N2 calls the battle the Helgeå, 'probably in 1026'), Pomerania and Orkney (N1 silent), the date of Magnus's recall beyond N1's 1034. Scania and Schleswig: N1 has Schleswig ceded back to Denmark during Cnut's 1027 Rome visit (undated further) and no firm Scanian date. The vassal tie with the Scottish kings is read as the Kingdom of Alba; Cliopatria's Alba row is a single shape through 1033 and another from 1034.
NORWAY is recorded as an occupation (hatched), not a gain, to match the old-kingdom-of-norway dossier's occupation_start 1028 and occupation_end 1035 for counterpart north-sea-empire; Cliopatria's Old Kingdom of Norway shape (1015-1039) lies under the empire's 1028-1035 Norway. ENGLAND: the kingdom-of-england dossier records England merged into the empire in 1018 and regained from denmark-england in 1042, with no 1035 event; here England separates from Denmark in 1035 (Harold Harefoot: regent 1035-1037, king until 1040, N2) and rejoins Denmark under Harthacnut in June 1040 (denmark-england). The two readings differ for 1035-1040 and need a reviewer.
NEW SLUGS: none. Counterparts needing dossiers: none beyond those already in polities.csv.
